title: Approval signoff metadata ledger — PRD (early draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc outlines an early PRD for a lightweight, verifiable "signoff metadata ledger" to attach to audit logs and approval gates for customer-managed networking (VPC/on‑prem). The goal is to provide compact, signed evidence about who authorized an action, what justification was used, and the operator context — without forcing full log duplication or heavy telemetry ingestion on the customer's side.

Background / Why this matters:
- Customers running Private deployments repeatedly ask for: auditable proof of operator approval, compact evidence artifacts to hand to internal security reviews, and a low-bandwidth way to retain forensics across intermittent on‑prem connectivity.
- Existing designs either keep large blobs (too much cost/retention), or minimal flags (not enough evidence for compliance). We need middle ground: compact, verifiable metadata that rides with the audit event and can be expanded for deeper forensics.

Design goals (must):
1) Compactness: each signoff artifact should be <= 2KB when base64-encoded in typical cases.
2) Verifiability: cryptographically signed (customer KMS or Redwood delegated key) and time-stamped.
3) Attachability: can be referenced/embedded in existing audit log formats (JSON-lines, syslog, CloudTrail-like).
4) Optional detail expansion: link to richer evidence (screenshots, attestation blobs) stored in customer-controlled storage or Redwood escrow if requested.
5) Minimal UX friction: operator experience to capture justification should be 2 lines + optional tags.
6) Privacy/GDPR: avoid storing PII in the compact token; support redaction.

Core artifact: Signoff Metadata Token (SMT) — example structure (human-readable pseudo-JSON for clarity):

  {
    "v": "1",                      // version
    "id": "smt_20240918_01",      // unique short id
    "actor": "ops-alice@cust.com",// short principal id (allowed hashed form)
    "action": "vpc-change:egress-rule-add",
    "justification": "permit-analytics-egress:legal-approval-ref-PR-34",
    "tags": ["scheduled-maintenance","low-risk"],
    "ts": "2024-09-18T15:22:03Z",
    "sig": "BASE64_SIG",           // signature over canonicalized payload
    "exp": "2024-12-18",          // optional retention/expires date
    "proof_url": "https://s3.cust/…/evidence-1234" // optional richer evidence link
  }

Notes: the above will be canonicalized and signed. The canonicalization rule must be stable across SDKs and server-side verifiers. We propose using JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) + SHA-256 + customer KMS (or Redwood service key when delegated) for signature.

APIs and storage model:
- CreateSignoff (operator flow): UI or CLI triggers CreateSignoff with minimal fields (action, justification, tags). Returns SMT token string and SMT id.
- AttachSignoff (audit instrumentation): When emitting audit event, recorder includes smt_id and optionally the full SMT token (configurable).
- VerifySignoff (forensics): Verifier checks signature, timestamp, and optional proof_url resolution.
- ListSignoffs (audit query): query by smt_id, actor, action, time window.

Operational modes (customer opt-in):
A) Inline mode: full SMT token is included in audit event. Simple, best UX, higher payload.
B) Reference mode: only smt_id is included; SMT is stored in a compact index (customer-owned bucket or Redwood encrypted store) and fetched only during investigation. Saves runtime bandwidth.

Retention & compliance knobs:
- Default SMT retention = 90 days for lightweight mode; 1 year for regulated customers (configurable).
- Support short-term TTL + legal-hold override.
- SMT content should not contain raw PII. If operator enters PII, SDK auto-hashes or rejects field.

Approval-gate UX sketches (operator):
- Web/CLI quick flow: 1) Select change action 2) Enter 1-line justification 3) Add risk tags (auto-suggest) 4) Optionally attach evidence link 5) Click sign -> SMT returned.
- Mobile/Slack flow: ephemeral signoff link with OAuth and 2FA enforced for high-risk tags.

Edge cases / Threats:
- Replay: SMTs must include nonce and timestamp. Verifiers check replay windows.
- Key compromise: support key rotation and signature versioning; older SMTs must remain verifiable via archived public keys and key rotation metadata.
- Offline operator: SDKs must locally cache SMTs until connectivity to store is available; attach smt_id and local cipher blob that is reconciled on next connection.

Integration with customer-managed networking:
- During VPC handover, operator creates SMT for allowed routes/peering changes. The SMT id is recorded in the customer change ticket and in the VPC change event.
- For on‑prem air‑gapped environments, our Private deploy agent should maintain an append-only SMT index (compact) on the customer side; Redwood can offer an escrowed signed digest for cross-org audits.

Monitoring & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (research): small internal pilot with SRE and 2 customer POCs — gather median SMT size and operator time-to-sign.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable Inline mode for 3 customers, default retention 90d, optional proof_url.
- Phase 2 (GA): support reference mode, KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM via PKCS#11), legal-hold, API quotas and billing.

Open questions (to resolve in next sprint):
- Canonicalization standard: JCS vs. custom stable ordering? (technical spike needed)
- Signature model: customer KMS-signature vs. customer-provided certs vs Redwood-signed delegated keys (tradeoffs for trust and ease).
- UX for redaction: how much operator-provided detail do we allow? need product/legal guidance.
- SMT query performance: reference mode requires fast index; where to host for Private customers?

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Spike: implement JCS canonicalizer in node/python SDKs + sample sign/verify (owner: Evan).
- Security review: draft key-rotation/compromise playbook (owner: Marta).
- Customer outreach: test flow with 2 customers in sales pipeline (owner: Samir).
- Infra scoping: storage cost model for inline vs reference modes (owner: Eng infra lead TBD).

Appendix: quick example audit line (JSON-lines style with inline SMT):

2024-09-18T15:22:03Z \u007b"event":"vpc.change","action":"egress-rule-add","resource":"vpc-123","actor":"operator:alice","smt":"eyJ2IjoiMSIsImlkIjoic210XzIwMjQwOTE4XzAxIiwiYWN0aW9uIjoi..."}

Notes to reviewers: this is early draft. Focus feedback on: minimal fields required for verifiability, retention knobs, and trust/signature model. If you have compliance examples from customers (SOC2, PCI, FedRAMP) that require specific fields in signoff evidence, paste them into comments below.

-- Priya
